sn9.5:1.2: The word “persuasion” (_saññatti_) is used in the context of discussions with skeptical non-Buddhists (eg. [mn60:8.5]()).
sn9.5:1.3: The same verse is spoken by a certain Vajjiputta (“Vajjian”) at [thag1.119](). The Pali commentary says this occurred shortly after the Buddha’s passing. Ānanda, still only a stream-enterer, was striving for arahantship before the First Council, but got caught up in consoling the distraught layfolk. The Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya agrees, adding that Vajjiputta was Ānanda’s attendant at the time. Following the exhortation Ānanda meditated to exhaustion, and when he finally say down to rest, he became awakened (Rockhill, *The Life of the Buddha*, p. 155).
sn9.5:2.2: Both Bodhi here and Norman in the parallel in *Elders Verses* ([thag1.119:1.2]()) read _osiya_ (“having placed”), which agrees with the commentarial gloss.
